title: [LeftBlock] `leftblock verify-ci` and a pre-push guard: no push to main without a receipt for the pushed SHA
description:
Repo: DataParade-io/LeftBlock. Files: `leftblock/ci.py`, `leftblock/hooks.py` (pre-push hook template, installed by `leftblock install --local --check-only --pre-push` or a new `--ci-guard` flag), `features/ci_guard.feature`, README.

`leftblock verify-ci --sha <sha> [--require-signature] [--status-only]`:
- Looks up the local receipt `.git/leftblock/receipts/<sha>.json`; if absent, queries `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<sha>/status` for context `leftblock/ci` (`--status-only` skips the local file; this is the mode the Amplify build uses with a token instead of gh — provide `--token-env GITHUB_TOKEN` or plain `curl` fallback so it runs without gh).
- `--require-signature` recomputes the HMAC with `LEFTBLOCK_SECRET_PATH` and fails on mismatch.
- Exit 0 only for `success`; print the receipt summary.

Pre-push guard (`.git/hooks/pre-push`): for each ref being pushed to `refs/heads/main`, run `leftblock verify-ci --sha <local sha>`; refuse with a message that says exactly what to run (`leftblock ci`). Merges done through the GitHub UI create a new SHA without a receipt, so the README states the private-repo rule: merge locally (fast-forward or local merge), run `leftblock ci` on the result, push. Protected branch list configurable (`ci.protected_branches: [main]`).
Gherkin: push to main with receipt passes; without receipt refused; push to a feature branch never checked; verify-ci against a fake status API.
